name: Advanced Material Characterization Techniques
description: Introduction to the working principles and data interpretation of a range of material characterization techniques—including BET surface area and pore analysis, x-ray diffraction (XRD), goniometry, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), raman spectroscopy, FTIR, NMR, UV-vis spectroscopy, dynamic light scattering (DLS), and microscopy methods such as SEM, TEM, AFM, and confocal microscopy, as well as photoluminescence quantum yield. It also covers thermal techniques like DSC and TGA, and mechanical testing using systems like Instron. The focus is on developing a strong foundation in quantitative analysis for understanding material properties across scales, enabling advancements in both research and industrial applications.
